literal: To friendship, the limb is intimate familiarity; and to that, being the seasoning salt is the duty of the noble.
translation: Intimate familiarity is the very life-limb of friendship; to be the seasoning salt that makes this familiarity sweet is the duty of the noble.
modern: நட்பிற்கு நெருங்கிய உரிமை பாராட்டுவதே சிறந்த உறுப்பாகும்; அந்த உரிமைக்கு இன்பம் தரும் உப்பாக விளங்குவது சான்றோரின் கடமையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the essence of long-standing friendship. The word 'keḻutakaimai' refers to the right of familiarity, where friends can act with freedom without needing formal permission. The poet states that this familiarity is the 'uṟuppu' (the vital limb or constituent) of friendship. To make this familiarity pleasant and enduring, noble friends must act as 'uppu' (salt or seasoning), gracefully accepting and returning this intimacy to keep the relationship flavorful and sweet.
